fineTune.title: Fine tuning
fineTune.description: Name format, preferred languages, accepted qualities — adapt every detail to your workflow.
fineTune.extendedDescription: Take complete control over your library's organization. Define custom folder structures (e.g., 'Movies/Year/Title'), prioritize specific audio languages, and filter out low-quality files. Your library, your exact rules.

xmlExport.title: Automatic pipeline mode
xmlExport.description: Drop a folder, the app renames, fetches subtitles and moves files to your final library on its own.
xmlExport.extendedDescription: Automate your post-download workflow. Pipeline Mode lets you set up a chain of actions: drop a folder, let CineRename identify the media, fetch matching subtitles from OpenSubtitles, rename with your selected preset, and move ready files to your NAS or final Plex library.

cli.title: CLI, Scheduler & NAS Docker
cli.description: Script your servers, schedule tasks (cron), or run CineRename in headless mode on your NAS or Docker container.
cli.extendedDescription: For power users and sysadmins, CineRename offers a robust Command Line Interface (CLI). Schedule renaming tasks using cron jobs, integrate it into your custom scripts, or deploy it as a headless Docker container on your Synology or Unraid NAS for 24/7 automated library management.

dryRunReport.title: Exportable dry-run reports
dryRunReport.description: Test your renaming rules safely and export the results to CSV/JSON without modifying a single file.
dryRunReport.extendedDescription: Perfect for complex media setups and cautious users. Run a 'Dry-Run' simulation to see what CineRename would do with your files without actually touching them. You can export this comprehensive summary as a CSV or JSON report to audit the planned changes, share with your team, or review offline.

watchFolders.title: Watch Folders
watchFolders.description: CineRename listens to your download folders and automatically imports new video files as soon as they appear.
watchFolders.extendedDescription: Let CineRename do the work while you sleep. Simply set up specific 'Watch Folders' (like your Torrent or Usenet download directories). CineRename runs silently in the background, instantly detecting when a new video file finishes downloading. It immediately processes, renames, and moves the file to your library without any manual input.

checksums.title: Checksum Verification
checksums.description: Check transfer integrity with native support for .sfv, .md5, and .sha1 files before organizing your library.
checksums.extendedDescription: Data corruption is the enemy of any media archivist. Before moving massive multi-gigabyte 4K releases, CineRename can read companion .sfv, .md5, and .sha1 files. It verifies the file hash so you can spot corruption before moving the video into your library.

localProcessing.title: Your files never leave your machine
localProcessing.description: No upload, no cloud. Only configured metadata and subtitle providers are contacted.
localProcessing.extendedDescription: Your privacy and data sovereignty are respected. CineRename processes all your video files locally on your own CPU. We never upload your files to the cloud. Network requests are limited to configured providers such as TheTVDB, TVmaze, AniList, Kitsu or OpenSubtitles.

parallelProcessing.title: Rust + Svelte 5 performance
parallelProcessing.description: Virtualized lists: stay smooth with thousands of files. Native Rust code for disk operations.
parallelProcessing.extendedDescription: Built from the ground up using a high-performance Rust backend and a lightning-fast Svelte 5 frontend. CineRename utilizes parallel multi-threading to process thousands of files simultaneously. Virtualized lists ensure the UI never lags, even when you load a massive 10TB media collection.

audioVideoSync.title: Subtitle matching
audioVideoSync.description: Built-in OpenSubtitles module: file fingerprint first, metadata fallback, preview, download and naming.
audioVideoSync.extendedDescription: Tired of subtitles that are out of sync by 2 seconds? CineRename integrates the OpenSubtitles API, searches by file fingerprint first, then falls back to title and metadata IDs. You can preview the subtitle before downloading it, and adjust offset or drift when a release needs a timing fix.

repetitionRemover.title: Duplicate hunter
repetitionRemover.description: Automatically detects multi-quality copies (1080p, 4K…), suggests the best version and frees disk space.
repetitionRemover.extendedDescription: Stop wasting precious hard drive space. When parsing your library, CineRename intelligently detects if you have multiple versions of the same movie or episode (e.g., a 720p version and a 4K HDR version). It suggests keeping only the highest quality file and safely archiving or deleting the duplicates.

multilingual.title: Multilingual, multi-format
multilingual.description: French, English, Spanish, Chinese — MKV, MP4, AVI, MOV — movies, TV shows, anime: all handled.
multilingual.extendedDescription: Whether you are organizing Hollywood blockbusters, French cinema, Spanish telenovelas, or Japanese Anime, CineRename handles it seamlessly. It supports all major video formats (MKV, MP4, AVI, MOV) and can search metadata in your native language so your Plex posters are localized.

blazingPreview.title: Instant before/after preview

blazingPreview.extendedDescription: No more blind renaming mistakes. The interactive Studio dashboard shows you exactly what your files will look like before any changes are committed to the disk. View the old filename side-by-side with the new Plex-compliant filename, ensuring 100% confidence before you hit 'Apply'.

about.title: Who builds CineRename?
about.description: CineRename is built by a cinephile tired of renaming files by hand and seeing Plex flag half their TV shows as 'unknown'.
about.quote: "I built CineRename because I wanted to watch a movie, not spend the evening fixing filenames."

items.v20: 🔜 v0.3 — Release packaging + direct updater channels
items.v22: 🔜 v0.5 — Metadata and subtitle matching polish

0.q: How does it compare to FileBot or TinyMediaManager?
0.a: CineRename was built from the ground up in Rust to be lightning-fast. Unlike older Java-based tools, it can process thousands of files without UI lag. We also built features that are usually missing: native ZIP/RAR extraction, an interactive visual preview, a full 'Undo' history, and multi-quality duplicate hunting.

1.a: Yes. CineRename supports anime presets with absolute episode numbering or season/episode output, plus OVA and Specials handling. For long shows where platforms disagree on seasons, you can keep absolute numbering and still fetch localized episode titles when available.

2.q: Do I have to pay a monthly subscription?
2.a: No. While we offer a yearly license for updates, we also provide a one-time 'Lifetime' payment option. We hate subscription fatigue as much as you do.

3.q: Will my files be uploaded to the cloud?
3.a: No. CineRename processes your files locally. Network requests only go to configured metadata and subtitle providers, and they contain titles, IDs, language choices, or the OpenSubtitles file fingerprint — never the video file itself.

4.q: Can it help find subtitles matching my release?
4.a: CineRename gives you the best possible match without promising magic. It uses the OpenSubtitles file fingerprint first, then falls back to title and metadata IDs. You can preview the subtitle before downloading it, and timing tools are available if a release still needs an offset or drift adjustment.

5.q: Why use CineRename instead of Sonarr/Radarr?
5.a: Sonarr and Radarr are amazing for full automation, but they require significant setup (indexers, download clients). CineRename is a lightweight, standalone tool. If you have an existing messy hard drive or just want to quickly organize files without running a 24/7 server, CineRename does the job instantly via Drag & Drop.

6.q: Does it run on my Headless NAS (Synology, Unraid)?
6.a: Yes. CineRename has a lightweight headless CLI, WebUI/TUI modes and Docker packaging. On servers, use the scheduler, cron, or download-client hooks; desktop Watch Folders remain available in the GUI app.

7.q: What happens if I make a mistake and rename thousands of files poorly?
7.a: Don't panic! CineRename tracks every operation in its History module. With a single click, you can undo a massive batch rename, and all your files will be restored to their original names and locations.

8.q: How will I receive my Pro license?
8.a: After purchase, you will immediately receive a license key by email. Simply enter it into the application to unlock the Pro version.
